That's true. I don't know if it's possible to fix. One workaround would be to use actionButton for everything, as it's inherently more flexible.

But I think a better question is, why is your entire UI wrapped in uiOutput? There are serious downsides to such an approach and many scenarios that previously required uiOutput are now achievable without it. If you could describe what you're doing we might be able to help you do it an easier way.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: submit button does not hold value change events when the button is generated on server side
parts:
actionButton works multiple times. You use it like this:

observe({
  if (input$myActionButton == 0)
    return()
  isolate({
    # Run your code here
  })
})

Or like this:

output$myPlot <- renderPlot({
  if (input$myActionButton == 0)
    return(NULL)
  isolate({
    # Do your plotting here
  })
})

The hardest thing will be figuring out how to add additional tabs at runtime. The tabsetPanel control that comes out-of-the-box with Shiny doesn't currently support adding tabs at runtime. You would have to either extend the existing tabsetPanel control using JavaScript, or write your own.

messages.subject: Re: submit button does not hold value change events when the button is generated on server side
parts:
I came up with a not-too-ugly way to have a spinner on top of the plot, it only includes a few CSS rules and a couple HTML elements.  I made it available in a gist
https://gist.github.com/daattali/edd7c20cd09f484b7f32

The main idea is to place a spinner image in the same container as the plot and center it, but give it a below-default z-index. Whenever the plot is recalculting, make the plot's z-index even lower so that the spinner will show.
 
I hope it makes sense and you find it useful
